correctness.rationale: The interval inequality description is equivalent to cyclic difference feasibility. Normal lengths give the exact maximum ball radius and inequalities for all optimal centers. For odd cycles, tight balanced intervals force zero by gcd rigidity. For even cycles, tight balanced intervals force two-periodicity and near-balanced intervals force singleton bounds; convexity proves these are sufficient for every remaining interval. Intersection-of-cube vertex enumeration gives the exact count. All quantifiers n>=3 and k>=2 and endpoint equalities are covered; standard-library checker corroborates small n with exact linear ranks and high precision inequalities.

value.rationale: This solves the natural full Chebyshev-center classification for a canonical infinite family, not merely an arbitrary numerical case or the already-known inradius: unique centers in odd cycles versus positive-dimensional cube-section loci in every even cycle, with explicit coordinate threshold and exact vertex counts. The proof also collapses the full set of cyclic support constraints to a simple exact description, a structural contribution useful for metric studies of graph polytopes.
